prompt: Build a fixed-capacity cache that evicts the least recently USED entry, where both reads and writes count as a use. Complete LruEvictionCache in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A LinkedHashMap remembers insertion order, so removing a key and putting it straight back moves it to the end -- that single trick turns insertion order into recency order, and the first key in the key set is then always the least recently used. Both get (on a hit) and put must perform that refresh, which is the difference between an LRU cache and a plain FIFO one. Eviction only happens on the path that adds a genuinely new key to a full cache, so an overwrite or a missed lookup must be careful not to take it.
hints: Store the entries in a LinkedHashMap. To mark a key as just used, remove it and put it back -- that moves it to the end of the iteration order.
keysLeastRecentFirst is then simply a copy of the key set, and the eviction victim is the first key that iterator gives you.

Split put into two cases before you touch anything: if the key is already present, refresh it and overwrite; only when it is new AND the cache is full do you remove the oldest key and bump the eviction counter.
